findings.title: Team admin/owner authorization requires both roles instead of either
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A team admin who is not the owner (and vice versa) therefore fails this check and, unless they are also the organizer or an attendee, gets FORBIDDEN when adding guests to a team booking they administer. The two checks must be combined with OR, as team admin and team owner are alternative privileged roles.

findings.title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests and modify the organizer's calendar event
findings.body: Authorization succeeds if the caller's email merely matches any existing attendee (`isAttendee`). That grants a non-organizer guest write access to the booking: they can add unlimited arbitrary people, who are persisted as attendees, receive scheduled-event emails/ICS invites, and are pushed to the organizer's calendar via updateCalendarAttendees. The bookings UI only exposes this to the booking owner/team, so the API is substantially more permissive than the intended organizer/team-admin surface.

findings.title: No booking status or timing check before adding guests
findings.body: After only checking the booking exists, the handler creates attendees, updates the calendar event, and sends invite/update emails. It never rejects CANCELLED, REJECTED, PENDING, or already-ended bookings. The UI also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings (bookedActions are shown for isBookingInPast && isConfirmed), so guests can be added to meetings that will not happen or have already happened, corrupting attendee lists and generating spurious calendar invites and emails.

findings.title: Duplicate and blacklist filtering is case-sensitive and intra-request duplicates are not removed
findings.body: uniqueGuests compares `guest === attendee.email` with exact case, compares the raw guest against a lower-cased blacklist (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lower-casing guest), and never de-duplicates the guests array against itself; the server schema also has no uniqueness refine (only the client does). Sending `A@x.com` plus `a@x.com`, an already-attending email with different casing, or the same email twice via a direct tRPC call creates duplicate Attendee rows and duplicate invites, and a differently-cased blacklisted address bypasses the blacklist.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, even though the booking (including `booking.user.credentials`/`destinationCalendar`) belongs to the organizer loaded from booking.userId. When a team admin/owner (or attendee) adds guests, the code tries to update the calendar event with the caller's credentials, so the organizer's calendar is not updated (or another user's calendar integration is used). It should load and use the booking organizer's user/credentials, as the booking owner is whose calendar holds the event.

findings.title: Emails are sent for the unfiltered guest list rather than the guests actually added
findings.body: The handler filters the request to uniqueGuests (removing existing attendees and blacklisted addresses) and persists only those, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered list. In email-manager that list decides who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail by `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so a pre-existing attendee whose email was re-submitted (and thus not newly added) incorrectly receives a fresh scheduled/invite email, and the new-vs-existing distinction is wrong whenever filtering removed anything. Pass uniqueGuests instead.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type disabled-email settings
findings.body: Unlike the neighbouring sendLocationChangeEmails/sendScheduledEmails, sendAddGuestsEmails never checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail and takes no eventTypeMetadata parameter. Event types that configured disableStandardEmails (all.host / all.attendee) will still emit organizer emails, team-member emails, and attendee emails for added guests, violating the event type's email-suppression contract.

findings.title: Guest list has no size limit, enabling attendee/email spam
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no .min(1)/.max() bound. A single authorized (including merely-attendee, per the handler) call can create an unbounded number of Attendee rows and trigger a calendar update plus an email/ICS to every address, making the endpoint usable for bulk unsolicited invites and resource exhaustion. Bound the array (and reject empty arrays explicitly rather than via the misleading uniqueness error).

findings.title: MultiEmail imports @calcom/ui from inside the ui package, creating a circular import
findings.body: This file lives in packages/ui and is exported from packages/ui/index.tsx via MultiEmailLazy, yet it imports Button, EmailField, Icon and Tooltip from "@calcom/ui" (the package's own barrel) instead of relative component paths. That creates a self-referential/circular dependency through the barrel (which also loads the lazy MultiEmail), risking undefined components at runtime and defeating the lazy-loading/bundle-splitting purpose stated in MultiEmailLazy. Import from the relative component modules like other form components in this package do.
